finding.root_cause: In the TryFrom<&AccountInfo> implementation for Program<T>, the id of T is compared with Pubkey::default() to decide whether any executable account is allowed; T defaults to () whose Id::id() returns Pubkey::default(), and System's id is also Pubkey::default(), so T=() and T=System behave identically and both accept any executable account.
finding.severity_source: severity published by Anchor advisory GHSA-c6rc-8jpp-2fgc (publisher GitHub user jamie-osec), CVSS 3.1 score 8.2; NVD republishes HIGH 8.2
finding.summary: Because Program<'a, ()> and the system program both compare equal to Pubkey::default(), Program<'info, System> accepts any executable account, so programs that assume they hold the real system program can be made to CPI elsewhere.
finding.title: Program<'info, System> accepts any program id, enabling arbitrary CPI or payment bypass in Anchor programs

finding.root_cause: Uint/Int pow and unary neg implementations use wrapping arithmetic rather than checked arithmetic, so overflow is silent for the affected widths.
finding.severity_source: severity published in CosmWasm advisory CWA-2024-002 (Medium, ACMv1 framework); the RustSec mirror carries no severity of ours
finding.summary: Some mathematical operations in cosmwasm-std use wrapping math instead of panicking on overflow for very big numbers, so contracts can compute wrong results.
finding.title: Arithmetic overflows in cosmwasm-std integer types silently wrap instead of panicking

finding.root_cause: CosmWasm's gas pricing benchmarks understate the real cost of certain Wasm operations, so the enforced gas target is missed by a factor of roughly ten.
finding.severity_source: severity published in CosmWasm advisory CWA-2024-004 as 'Medium (Moderate + Likely)' under ACMv1; the wasmvm GitHub advisory independently records medium
finding.summary: Some Wasm operations cost far more gas than the benchmarks used for pricing, so a malicious contract can execute for about ten times longer than the gas target and temporarily DoS a chain.
finding.title: Gas mispricing in cosmwasm-vm lets a contract run about ten times longer than the gas target

root_cause.note: paraphrased from the post-mortem we fetched and read
root_cause.value: price staleness in Levana's Pyth integration (120 second staleness window, deviation-gated updates) combined with an Osmosis fee-market/congestion condition that blocked user and bot transactions; the post-mortem states there is no vulnerability in Pyth itself

severity.note: no severity rating is published; the post-mortem instead publishes a loss estimate of $1.146M, roughly 10% of the funds in Levana's liquidity pools over the attack window, with per-market losses listed (stATOM $241k, ATOM $229k, BTC $190k, ETH $128k, TIA $108k, *_USDC $168k + $82k)

affected_components: Levana Perps market contracts on Osmosis
finding.root_cause: Price updates are only pushed when the price deviates or on a cadence, and the market contract's updates become stale after 120 seconds; combined with insufficient gas prices during an Osmosis congestion episode, Levana's bots and users could not land updates, leaving a window in which an attacker could trade against a stale price.
finding.severity_source: no severity rating published by the post-mortem
finding.summary: Levana market contract price updates go stale after a 120 second lag while a congestion/fee-market problem stopped users and bots from landing transactions, so attackers could open positions on an old price and close on the new one, draining roughly 10% of pool funds over 13 days.
finding.title: Stale Pyth oracle prices plus chain congestion let attackers drain about $1.146M from Levana LPs over 13 days
